title: Taiwan’s Tech Diplomacy Has a Labor Problem
author: Ethan Chiu
text:
Foreign migrant workers often gather in the square in front of Taipei Station during their day off. Photo taken Sep. 24, 2023.
Credit: Shutterstock
In an investigation published this October, three migrant workers at a Garmin factory in Taiwan said recruiters had forced them to sign documents falsely denying the mandatory fees they had paid to get jobs. Two reported that the recruiters threatened to retaliate and deport them if they disclosed the charges. These workers were making products for a U.S.-based electronics company.The nonprofit Transparentem interviewed 24 workers at seven manufacturers operating in Taiwan and documented recruitment fees totaling $6,400 each. Compal, the laptop maker, and Garmin claimed they had long prohibited worker-paid fees. But they only reimbursed current migrant workers after investigators contacted them, and excluded former workers from compensation. Despite corporate promises, these exploitative charges continued.[...]
